brief: JPMorgan Market Intelligence's September 14 afternoon briefing reports US stocks closed lower (SPX -0.5%, NDX -0.8%) because investors rotated out of AI picks-and-shovels names after Dario's AI pacing essay, into hyperscalers (GOOGL, META) and security software (CRWD, ZS, PANW), while the 10Y broke through 5% intraday before closing at 4.988% ahead of the September 16 FOMC. WTI rose 1.34% to $101.39. The bank's energy specialist sets a bull case (products positioning at the 90th-plus percentile, OVX near 60 versus 70 at past tantrum peaks, no demand destruction) against a bear case (seasonal gasoline step-down, Chinese buying above $100/bbl in doubt, a higher dollar from renewed hiking, oil demand 5mmbd below last year). JPM keeps a tactically cautious and neutral view into the Fed, stating this is not a fundamentally based view since macro and earnings (>20% EPS growth for 26Q3 and 26Q4) are supportive, but a 10Y cycle high, widening credit spreads and bond volatility take up to eight weeks for equities to digest. It would still buy the AI dip. Its updated midterm work concludes a strong pre-midterm rally does not reduce +3mo and +6mo post-midterm returns, though +12mo returns may be lower.
